data.name: Narahari
data.gender_notes: Narahari is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Narahari is a name derived from the Sanskrit words 'Nara' (man) and 'Hari' (Lord Vishnu). This name represents the form of Lord Vishnu who appears in the form of a man-lion. It is also a name of Lord Rama and Shiva. The name Narahari carries the meaning “Lord of the man-lion” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Narahari usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the man-lion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of divine protection and strength.
data.etymology: Narahari belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the man-lion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Narahari total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Narahari stands for the fusion of two powerful entities - the human and the divine. This name is deeply rooted in Hindu mythology and represents the victory of good over evil. In the Hindu epic Mahabharata, Lord Narasimha, the fourth avatar of Lord Vishnu, is shown saving Prince Hiranyakashipu's son, Prahlada, from his demon father. The story portrays the fierce manifestation of the deity in the form of a man-lion, thus creating a significant impact on Hindu culture and belief systems.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the name Narahari signifies divinity within humanity. It is a reminder that the divine and the human are not separate entities, but are interconnected. The name symbolizes the divine presence in all of us, the potential for us to overcome our individual challenges and evils, and the promise of the ultimate victory of good over evil. Narahari also represents the idea that true strength comes from within, and that we are all capable of accessing that inner power to protect and serve ourselves and others.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Narahari is a form of Vishnu, symbolizing the destructive aspect of God. His name means "Lord of the Man-lion," representing the fierce protector who vanquishes evil with unwavering courage.

historical_references.reference: Narahari is an avatar of the god Vishnu, specifically identified with the deity Narasimha. The name Narahari is derived from 'Nara' (man) and 'Hari' (God Vishnu). The legend of Narasimha is described in the Puranas, particularly the Bhagavata Purana, and is part of the larger Hindu epic Mahabharata.

Another reference to Narahari comes from the medieval Indian kingdom of Chalukya dynasty (566–1247 CE) in the Deccan Plateau. King Bijjala II (r. 1155–1173 CE), a Jaina king, is said to have taken the name 'Narahari' to honor the god Narasimha, in order to protect his kingdom from Muslim invaders.

modern_usage.modern_context: Narahari, an ancient Hindu deity, is gaining popularity in modern contexts for his unique characteristics and diverse interpretations. He is known as the 'Lord of the Forests', 'Slayer of Naraasura', and 'Protector of the Weak'. Narahari is worshipped in various forms such as Hari-Har, Narasimha, and Vishvarupa. In the digital space, Narahari is frequently discussed on Reddit threads dedicated to Hindu mythology and folklore. On Twitter, Hindu devotees share stories, rituals, and artwork related to Narahari. DeviantArt, a popular platform for digital art, has numerous pieces dedicated to Narahari, showcasing his various forms and symbolic meanings. These trends reflect the enduring relevance of Hindu mythology and the increasing interest in exploring its complexities in today's world.
